findings.issue: MigrateLegacyRows runs on every fsm command (roots()), never records completion, strictly parses the main checkout's live per-worktree .metareview/runs.jsonl, and for each fsm-* row calls Exists and appendRow (each re-reading the common ledger under flock).
findings.consequence: O(legacy rows x ledger rows) on every fsm command forever (measured ~16.5s per `fsm state` with 2000 legacy rows), and one malformed line in that review ledger (lock-free AppendJSONL writers) makes every fsm command in every worktree fail with an ERR_RUNS_JSONL that names the wrong file.

findings.issue: The shared-store abandoned scan keeps a run only when canonical(work_dir) equals this worktree's toplevel exactly; fsm init --work-dir accepts any directory inside a worktree, so a subdirectory work_dir (or a removed worktree's) matches no worktree. The legacy fallback reads the CURRENT worktree's .metareview/runs (not the main checkout's single 0.13.x location), unscoped and without a warning.
findings.consequence: An abandoned run started with --work-dir <subdir> is never reported anywhere (reproduced: status blocked:false), letting the Stop gate pass; from a linked worktree its unmigrated runs are invisible and from main other branches' runs can falsely block.

findings.issue: writeFSMRun and the shell mkfsmrun helpers still forge runs under <root>/.metareview/runs, so every passing record-lenses --from-run end-to-end test exercises only the 0.13.x fallback; the common-dir read path has no integration test.
findings.consequence: A regression in the primary record-lenses path passes CI; removing the fallback later breaks the suites wholesale.

findings.issue: TestFSMRootsAreDeclared (buildsRootedPath) and TestRunStoreReadersAreDeclared match only the .metareview spellings; neither sees the new "metareview", "runs" common-dir paths, and `root: store` now ambiguously means common dir or anchor.
findings.consequence: The tripwires no longer guard the store they exist for; a new undeclared or mis-rooted common-dir reader passes.

verdict.reasoning: The diff shows that each MigrateLegacyRows invocation reparses the legacy ledger and performs Exists plus appendRow for every fsm-* row, with no completion marker inside this function. However, it does not show roots() or any call site, so the central claim that this runs on every FSM command forever is unverified. The measured timing, lock-free writer behavior, and claim that the resulting error names the wrong file are also unsupported by the supplied evidence. Without the call path and error construction, the proposed command-wide regression cannot be confirmed from this diff alone.

The primary defect is real: the new shared-store filter uses exact canonical path equality (`canonical(r.workDir) == canonical(root)`). If init records an accepted subdirectory as `work_dir`, that run is excluded even though it belongs to the current worktree, so an abandoned run can be missed and the gate can pass. The additional claims about removed worktrees and the legacy store layout are not established by this diff, but they are not needed for the concrete subdirectory-scoping bug.

The finding is real based on the shown diff alone. The migration says current FSM data lives under <git-common-dir>/metareview, yet driving-a-workflow.md and skills/fsm/SKILL.md still document terminal rows at .metareview/runs.jsonl. The comment at cmd/metareview/main.go:529-530 also still says the run store is the main worktree, directly contradicting the new repo.StoreDir-based lookup. These stale statements can send readers and agents to the wrong location. The additional claims about unchanged files are not independently verifiable from this excerpt, but the visible contradictions are sufficient.

findings.issue: here := canonical(root) uses the repo.Root result, not git's show-toplevel, while runs are attributed by Toplevel(work_dir); a status root in a monorepo subdirectory carrying its own docs/metareview or .metareview never equals a run's toplevel.
findings.consequence: From such a subdirectory, status reports no abandoned runs, so the Stop gate can pass over an abandoned run.

findings.issue: In a bare repository with linked worktrees, repo.RunStoreRoot falls back to RootOr(root), which stops at a subdirectory with its own docs/metareview, while here is now the worktree's toplevel, so here != main in every worktree.
findings.consequence: A run whose worktree was removed is reported from no checkout in that bare-repo + monorepo-subdir layout. Canonicalising main through Toplevel too would restore symmetry.
